scenarios.name: bear
scenarios.drivers: AI capex digests after the Blackwell/Rubin cycle: FY2028 growth falls well short of the ~70% guided [R6] as Baird's softer-demand signals [R35] and weak cash conversion with receivables up [R40] show up, memory-cost pressure on $279bn of commitments [R27] and cheaper custom-chip alternatives [R74] hold gross margin near the trough [R5], and the CEO investigation [R57] and export-rule tightening [R49] add disruption. Probability: 25% because 1H growth and the Q3 guide [R1] anchor FY2027 and management's FY2028 guide [R6] and demand commentary [R33] are strong, but the governance and demand-visibility concerns [R35][R57] are real.

scenarios.name: base
scenarios.drivers: Revenue follows the Q3 guide of $108bn [R1] and management's ~70% FY2028 guide [R6] with Vera Rubin in full production [R33] and supply commitments in place [R27], while FCF margin sits below the 41.9% current level because gross margin troughs at 71-72% on memory costs [R5][R14] and cash conversion is held back by receivables [R40]. Probability: 55% because guidance [R6] and consensus agree on the path and 1H results [R20] support it, with risks from margins [R14] and visibility [R35] keeping it from being higher.

scenarios.name: bull
scenarios.drivers: Demand keeps accelerating as multiple frontier labs scale in parallel [R33], the $500bn third-party compute financing platforms [R62] and the OpenAI-linked PORTS-Pike build-out [R30] pull orders forward, and memory costs ease so gross margin recovers faster than the trough guide [R5] and cash conversion improves [R44]. Probability: 20% because it needs both faster growth than the ~70% guide [R6] and a margin rebound against the memory-cost headwind [R27], though demand signals [R33] and the supply commitments [R27] make it plausible.

scenarios.note: Assumptions set by our analyst step from the research notes and the debate; the base case's revenue growth is our forecast's; values computed in code with the model's DCF (WACC 11.9%, terminal growth 2.5%, same net debt and share count). After year 3 the growth above terminal growth halves each year. Bear and bull are kept at least a minimum distance from the base case, set from the company's own historical swings (revenue growth 40%, FCF margin 3% standard deviation); widened: bear FY2029 growth, bull FY2029 growth.

narrative.thesis: The stock turns on whether AI demand survives beyond the guided period. We say it does: first-half revenue rose 95.8%, Q3 is guided higher again, and management guides roughly 70% growth for FY2028, where our forecast sits just above consensus. At today's price the reverse DCF needs only 6.7% annual revenue growth from FY2029, against our 10.2%, on a forward P/E well below peers after a sharp de-rating. Quality is mixed — investment gains are about a fifth of net profit and cash conversion fell — and the CEO investigation is unquantified. Our probability-weighted scenarios give Buy at USD 200.02, low confidence; a heavier bear weight would move us to Hold.
key_takeaways: 1H FY2027 revenue rose 95.8% at a 75.0% gross margin; Q3 guided to $108.0bn with no China compute.
Management guides about 70% revenue growth for FY2028; our forecast is +70.0%, slightly above consensus.
The price implies 6.7% annual revenue growth from FY2029, below our base case's 10.2%.
Cash conversion fell to 0.63x and investment gains were about 20% of net profit.
Buy, fair value USD 200.02 (+18.4%); a heavier weight on the bear case would move us to Hold.
narrative.company_overview:
NVIDIA designs accelerated computing platforms — GPUs, networking and full AI systems — sold through two segments, Compute & Networking and Graphics, and increasingly as data-centre-scale AI factories rather than components. In FY2026 Data Center was 89.7% of revenue (193.7bn), Gaming 7.4%, Professional Visualization 1.5% and Automotive 1.1%; the United States took 69.3%, Taiwan 19.6% and Mainland China & Hong Kong 9.1%.

Customers are hyperscalers — about half of Data Center revenue — plus AI clouds, enterprises, sovereign programmes and, in gaming, consumer PC and workstation buyers. The edge is the CUDA software ecosystem and a one-year product cadence (Blackwell, Blackwell Ultra, now Vera Rubin), which support a 75.0% gross margin in 1H FY2027; the risk is that the same margin invites custom silicon from its largest buyers.
narrative.financial_analysis: 1H FY2027 revenue was 177,837mn, up 95.8% from 90,805mn, with gross margin of 75.0% against 66.6% and operating profit up 134.2%; the second quarter alone grew 105.9% to 96,221mn. We forecast FY2027 revenue of 411,794mn (+90.7%, in line with consensus), FY2028 of 700,049mn (+70.0%, +1.1% vs consensus, following management's ~70% guide) and FY2029 of 947,167mn (+35.3%). Gross margin falls to 73.7% and 71.5% as Q4 bottoms at 71-72% on memory costs, with 279bn of supply commitments. The five-year record is exceptional — FY2026 ROE 101.5% on a 55.6% net margin — but accruals (+10.9%) and receivable days (52; FY2025: 46) show the working-capital cost; net cash fell to 23,220mn at 26 Jul 2026 from 41,202mn in January, as debt rose 24,898mn and cash 6,916mn.
narrative.valuation_overview:
Our fair value of USD 200.02 is the probability-weighted scenario value: bear USD 77.20 (25%), base USD 206.69 (55%) and bull USD 335.19 (20%). The mechanical DCF gives USD 219.03; the value bridge explains the gap: a lower FCF margin (40% base against the model's 43.3%) costs 14.87 per share, more than our higher revenue adds, on memory costs and receivables.

The reverse DCF shows the price implies 6.7% annual revenue growth from FY2029 to FY2036 against our 10.2%, so the market discounts a slower path than we forecast. Peer forward P/E (10.6x vs a 20.4x median) points far higher and sits outside the rating; the P/E on last year's EPS, 34.5x, is in the 4th percentile of five years; the Monte Carlo median is USD 216.08 with 66% of draws above the price. Low confidence reflects the 43% scenario spread and the peer gap; a higher weight on the bear case would move us to Hold.
narrative.competitive_analysis: Against Broadcom, AMD, Marvell and QUALCOMM, NVIDIA's latest-quarter revenue growth of 105.9% compares with a peer median of 40.6%, its 65.2% operating margin with 19.3%, and its 117.2% ROE with 30.4%. Gross margin of 74.7% is near Broadcom's 75.5% and far above AMD's 56.0%. Yet the shares trade at 10.6x forward earnings against a 20.4x peer median: the market prices NVIDIA as the cyclical, not the franchise.
narrative.news_summary: News is dominated by governance. On 8 November the company said it had opened an investigation into reports that a foreign intelligence operation targeted CEO Jensen Huang; the Wall Street Journal then reported, after the price date, that the board is preparing to oust him. Aletheia Capital cut to Hold. Separately, the Justice Department is scrutinising the Hugging Face acquisition and new export rules require partners to curb sales to Chinese clients. Product news is positive — Huang's deployment blueprint and a Vertiv partnership — but the shares fell 9.3% on 5 November amid a Nasdaq correction and 5.5% more on 10 November.
narrative.report_summary:
On 26 August 2026 management guided Q3 FY2027 revenue to $108.0bn ±2% with no Data Center compute revenue from China assumed, gross margin of 74.0% ±50bp and GAAP opex of about $9.2bn; on the call it said fourth-quarter gross margin should bottom at 71-72% on memory costs and guided fiscal 2028 growth of about 70%. Supply and capacity commitments rose to $279 billion.

On 2 September 2026 it agreed to buy Hugging Face for about $11.9 billion, closing in the first half of 2027, and on 28 September added a $150 billion buyback authorisation, lifting remaining capacity to $235 billion. New export rules require cloud partners to take at least 51% of future sales from non-Chinese buyers, and Baird warns an H200 ban could cost a US$5 billion inventory write-down. The 10-Q flags $108.5bn of guarantees; the 10-K's risk factors centre on supply lead times, foundry dependency and competition.

learner.big_picture:
NVIDIA designs AI chips, mostly for data centers. Sales are growing very fast: first-half revenue rose 95.8% on a year earlier. Management guides about 70% growth for FY2028. The share price has fallen, partly because a board inquiry into the CEO worries investors. Our model rating is Buy at USD 200.02, with low confidence. Profit quality is mixed: investment gains are about a fifth of net profit, and cash conversion fell. A heavier bear weight would move the rating to Hold.

steps.business: NVIDIA sells AI chips and systems. Data Center is 89.7% of FY2026 revenue, so one customer group, the builders of AI computing centers, drives almost everything. The United States is 69.3% of sales. Gaming is small by comparison. Which segment is the second largest?
steps.growth: The latest quarter, up 105.9% on a year earlier, is faster than the first half at +95.8%. That means growth is speeding up. Consensus (the average analyst forecast) expects FY2027E revenue growth of +90.7%, with revenue of USD 411.9bn. Growth in the FY2026 year was +65.5%. Is the latest quarter faster or slower than the first half?
steps.profit: Operating margin (operating profit per 100 of sales, before interest and tax) rose from 37.3% to 60.4% over FY2022 to FY2026. Cash conversion of 0.86x means each 1.00 of profit brought in less cash. In the first half it was 0.63x, so check the cash flow statement. What was FY2026 cash conversion?
steps.safety: NVIDIA holds more cash than debt, called net cash. At 26 Jul 2026, cash and marketable securities were USD 56,586mn and net cash was USD 23,220mn. Net cash was USD 41,202mn at FY2026 year-end, so it fell, because debt rose by USD 24,898mn. What was total debt at 26 Jul 2026?
steps.cheap: On trailing P/E (price divided by the last twelve months of profit per share) NVIDIA is 21.4x against a peer median of 49.8x, a discount. On P/B (price against the owners' book value) it is at a premium. P/E on last fiscal year's EPS is 34.5x, a different basis, so do not compare them. What is the peer median P/E?
steps.worth: Our fair value of USD 200.02 blends bear, base and bull cases by probability. The reverse DCF (working backward from the price to the growth it assumes) needs +6.7% a year from FY2029, below our +10.2%. Confidence is low because the scenarios are far apart. What are the bear and bull values?
steps.others: Brokers' median target is USD 319.50, far above our USD 200.02. Brokers are often positive, and 29 of 30 ratings here are Buy or Outperform. Check how old each target is (6 are older than 90 days) and what growth and multiple each assumes. How many targets are older than 90 days?
steps.wrong: The share price fell 14.9% over one year while the S&P 500 rose 10.1%. The largest peak-to-trough fall in the past year was 29.4%. A board inquiry into the CEO is a governance risk, and its outcome is unknown. Results on 17 Nov 2026 are the next test. What is the one-year volatility?

narrative.brief:
ANALYST BRIEF (the lead analyst's view, decided before writing: build the tagline, thesis, risks, valuation and rating text on it; every figure in it is from `facts`, `news` or `filings`):
- Central question: Does AI demand hold up after the guided ~70% FY2028 growth, and are the margin, cash-conversion and CEO-investigation worries already priced at USD 168.89?
- Our answer: Yes, on balance: Buy, fair value USD 200.02 (+18.4%), low confidence. 1H FY2027 revenue was 177,837mn (+95.8%), Q3 is guided to $108.0bn, and management guides ~70% FY2028 growth. The bear case, USD 77.20 at 25%, covers demand digestion and governance disruption.
- What the price implies: The price implies only 6.7% a year revenue growth from FY2029 to FY2036, against our base case of 10.2%. The forward P/E is 10.6x against a peer median of 20.4x, and the stock is down 25.0pp against the S&P 500 over one year. Consensus FY2028E EPS rose +24.1% in 90 days while the price fell: a de-rating, not lower estimates.
- Pillar 1: Demand is still accelerating and is covered by supply commitments. Evidence: Q2 Data Center revenue $89.0bn, +117% y/y; Q3 guide $108.0bn ±2%; supply and capacity commitments $279 billion versus $119 billion last quarter.. Breaks if: Q3 actuals or Q4 guidance fall short of the $108.0bn step-up, or Baird's softer-demand signals spread..
- Pillar 2: The price discounts far less growth than we forecast. Evidence: Reverse DCF implies 6.7% growth from FY2029 versus our 10.2%; forward P/E 10.6x versus peer median 20.4x; scenario value USD 200.02.. Breaks if: Growth after FY2028 fades below the 6.7% implied, as in our bear case (-4.7% in year 3)..
- Pillar 3: Margins and cash conversion are the weak spot, and we model them. Evidence: Q4 gross margin guided to 71-72% on memory costs; 1H cash conversion 0.63x versus 0.95x; guarantees USD 108.5bn; investment gains 23.7bn, about 20% of net profit.. Breaks if: Receivables keep absorbing cash or the OpenAI-linked guarantees are drawn..
- Beyond our forecast years: After FY2029 our value needs AI capex to keep compounding at about 10% a year with FCF margin near 40%. Bear drivers: custom-chip competition, a memory-cost squeeze, and customer financing risk. Bull drivers: a Vera Rubin cycle, $500bn of third-party compute financing, and a faster margin recovery.
- Revenue and profit quality: 1H FY2027 net profit of 118,010mn is 101% of operating profit; investment gains of 23.7bn are non-cash fair-value gains, so operating profit growth (+134.2%) is the true trend. Cash conversion fell to 0.63x from 0.95x. Receivable days were 52 in FY2026, up from 46. Guarantees reach USD 108.5bn.
- Governance: Management said, as reported by CNBC and Mint, that the board launched an independent investigation, led by Wachtell Lipton, into allegations about CEO Jensen Huang. The WSJ reported on 11 Nov, after the price date, that the board is preparing to oust him. The company has not confirmed that report. The outcome is unknown.
- Where we differ from the brokers: Our FY2027 and FY2028 numbers are within about 1% of consensus. The gap is in value: our USD 200.02 sits far below the brokers' median target of USD 319.50. We use a 40% FCF margin against 43.3% in the mechanical DCF, because of memory costs and receivables, and we put 25% on a bear case that includes governance risk.
- What to watch: Q3 results on 17 Nov 2026: guide revenue $108.0bn, gross margin 74.0%; consensus EPS 2.47. The options market prices ±9.7%. A Q4 guide below consensus's $124.7bn, a gross margin below 71%, or a CEO exit would push us towards Hold. The House briefing is on 18 Nov.
- Tagline (by the lead analyst; use it as the report's tagline as written): The market prices governance turmoil and an AI peak; the evidence says demand and cheap multiples still favour Buy.
- Thesis paragraph (by the lead analyst; use it as the thesis, changing only what a rule or `feedback` requires; a deep report adds one sentence on the debate's verdict and swing factor): The stock turns on whether AI demand survives beyond the guided period. We say it does: 1H FY2027 revenue rose 95.8%, Q3 is guided to $108.0bn, and management guides about 70% growth for FY2028. At USD 168.89 the price needs only 6.7% annual growth from FY2029, against our 10.2%, on a forward P/E of 10.6x. Quality is mixed: investment gains are about 20% of net profit and cash conversion fell to 0.63x. The CEO investigation is an unquantified risk. The rating is Buy, fair value USD 200.02, with low confidence, and it would fall to Hold if the bear probability rose from 25% to 29%. Brokers' median target is far higher; we are more cautious on margins.

company.description: NVIDIA Corporation operates as a data center scale AI infrastructure company in the United States, Taiwan, China, Hong Kong, Europe, and internationally. It operates through Compute & Networking, and Graphics segments. The Compute & Networking segment provides data center accelerated computing and networking platforms and artificial intelligence solutions and software, and automotive platforms and autonomous and electric vehicle solutions, including software. The Graphics segment offers GeForce GPUs for gaming and PCs; Quadro/NVIDIA RTX GPUs for enterprise workstation graphics. The company's products are used in gaming, professional visualization, data center, and automotive markets. It sells its products to original equipment manufacturers, original device manufacturers, system integrators and distributors, independent software vendors, cloud service providers, add-in board manufacturers, distributors, automotive manufacturers and tier-1 automotive suppliers, and other ecosystem participants. It has a collaboration with Cisco to develop Ultra-Dense Small Form Factor Pluggable (USFP), a high-density optical module pluggable transceiver. It has a collaboration with ChipAgents to develop Build-A-Chip-Bench, a benchmark for AI agents carrying chip design tasks and The Company has a strategic alliance with MediaTek to build the next generations of AI computing platforms. NVIDIA Corporation was incorporated in 1993 and is headquartered in Santa Clara, California.
